latest_substantive_result.summary: For a supplied finite class of deterministic total Mealy worlds with hidden anchors and a single action/output stream, the frozen theorem reports that behavior-preserving return tests compose and, under complete synthesis, arbitrary informative returning-test choices reach the unique class of worlds indistinguishable by every finite safe returning test in at most |B0|−1 successful stages. Pair-goal least-fixed-point synthesis has explicit node bound N≤∏w(1+n_w)−1 and may be exponential; the separate DFA-intersection reduction gives PSPACE-hardness, not a new exact complexity classification. A stipulated four-world mechanism check reports aa then a conditionally returning b test, four actions per world and measured symbolic search counts; a conventional strong planner independently finds the same full depth-four policy. Physical class/actions are not acquired, and no planner advantage or physical capability is established.

publication.scope: Exact finite deterministic total Mealy classes with a supplied finite pointed-world prior W, including the assumed membership of the actual system and allowed anchor set. The interface is one immutable action/output stream with no reset, state-label sensor, equivalence teacher or supplied experiment library. A return boundary requires current state to be behaviorally equivalent to that world's anchor, meaning identical output traces for every future action word. Let R(B0) be all finite returning adaptive tests valid at the initial returned belief B0; worlds are equivalent when every such test has the same transcript. Complete synthesis plus any informative returning test at each stage reaches exactly the actual world’s class under this relation in at most |B0|−1 successful stages. Pair-goal least-fixed-point synthesis uses goal=returned and selected pair separated, adds a node when one action sends every nonempty observation successor to the previous winning set, and has N≤∏_(w∈W)(1+n_w)−1 nonempty epistemic nodes. The supplied separate DFA-intersection reduction reports PSPACE-hardness under its explicit encoding; no exact general complexity classification follows. The four-world mechanism is a separately bounded stipulated class: aa costs two primitive actions and returns while revealing θ; then b plus the θ-dependent return action gives φ; source and target cost four primitive actions in each world. A conventional strong planner independently finds the same full depth-four policy. No physical class membership or physical actions are acquired, no planner advantage is claimed, and the separate Gaussian/death risk-limited research is not included.
